name: Paula

findings.what: Recusant count is 8 distinct passages, not 9: 1098 and 1101 sit in one sentence.

dates_source cites line 20122 as the Letter CVIII headnote. That line is the Letter XCIX (To Theophilus) headnote. It does mention grief for Paula's death in 404, but the CVIII headnote with 'recently died' and 'The date of the letter is 404' is at 20793-20807.
findings.fix: Cite 20807 for Letter CVIII, or describe 20122 as the Letter XCIX headnote.

findings.what: The hold reason frames Letter XLVI as an open question. As the qualifying test is written, a document issued in her name counts as own words, and the headnote says Jerome wrote it 'in the name of' Paula and Eustochium. So the letter qualifies on its face. What Mark actually has to decide is whether a ghost-written letter is enough, plus whether co-founding the Bethlehem houses makes her a founder. Hold is still right, but the question should be put that way.
findings.fix: Reword the reason so it puts both questions to Mark: is a ghost-written letter enough, and do the Bethlehem houses make her a founder.

why: The counts are sound and Letter XLVI does meet the wording of the test. But it was ghost-written and she co-founded the Bethlehem houses, so the call is Mark's.

name: Polycarp of Smyrna

rejected.van-braght_martyrs-mirror_sohm1886.txt:1: same paragraph as 14821 (continues across page break 14823-24)

findings.what: party_in_own_right says Eusebius and Socrates put him on one side of an Easter dispute 'with Victor of Rome'. Eusebius (HE V.24) and Socrates (V.22) both name Anicetus. Only Sozomen says Victor, and the edition's own note marks that as an error ('Not Victor, but Anicetus').
findings.fix: Say he met Anicetus of Rome over the Easter date (Eusebius HE V.24; Socrates V.22).

findings.what: The imperial quote is credited to 'Socrates V.22'. Line 41769 is Sozomen VII.19 (div1 3, id iii.xii.xix). Sozomen is on the same shelf, so the count holds. Socrates V.22 is line 16243.
findings.fix: Credit the quote to Sozomen VII.19, or quote Socrates at 16243.

findings.what: Three of the five imperial refs are Eusebius quoting Irenaeus or the Smyrnaean letter (22962, 23149, 23185). The rule allows them, but Eusebius's own narrative also names Polycarp in several more places, which makes the count sturdier.
findings.fix: Optionally swap in Eusebius's own sentences; the count does not change.

findings.what: The draft's Anabaptist count (8) treats the whole martyrdom account as one passage. That is stricter than the rule, which merges by paragraph. By paragraph the count is 11.

why: His letter is held on the home shelf, he founded nothing, and both later traditions clear 5 easily. Only the Victor/Anicetus error needs fixing.

name: Maximilla

rejected.epiphanius_panarion-haer-48-69-corpus-ha: same paragraph as 2948 (blank lines are OCR page artefacts)

findings.what: own_words says 'The Montanism shelf holds no Montanist own writing at all.' That is false. The shelf holds Tertullian's Montanist-period treatises as role tradition: Against Praxeas, De Fuga, De Exhortatione Castitatis, De Jejunio, De Pudicitia, De Monogamia and De Virginibus Velandis. The conclusion still stands, because none of these are hers.
findings.fix: Say: the shelf holds Montanist writing (Tertullian), but none by her; her oracles survive only as quotations by opponents.

findings.what: Palestinian count is 7 distinct passages, not 10: three refs share a paragraph with another ref.
Two imperial refs (29776, 29849) are Eusebius quoting the anonymous anti-Montanist. The rule allows them. Eusebius's own sentences at 29269 (HE V.14), 29825 and 29882 carry the count without them.
'Later writers name her whenever they argue about whether prophecy has ended' goes further than the cited texts show.
findings.fix: Say Epiphanius turns her saying that no prophetess would come after her against the movement.

why: No own words of hers are held: every saying comes through opponents. The co-prophet/founder question also stands.

name: Methodius of Olympus

rejected.nikon_replies-against-streshnev-and-liga: same paragraph as 21582 (one gloss paragraph on Rev 12:1, 21573-21620, across a page break)

findings.what: Russian count falls to 4: 21582 and 21617 are in one paragraph of the quoted gloss on Rev 12:1. I make it up with Nikon 5360, 'the treatise of Methodius, bishop of Patara, on Antichrist'. Nikon means Methodius of Olympus/Patara, though Palmer's appendix notes the work is pseudo-Methodius (34884). The Russian count therefore passes at exactly 5, and only if pseudonymous attributions count as naming him. The Liguori count already relies on that, since its Hypapante citations are pseudo-Methodian too. Nikon 7950 repeats the Rev 12:6 gloss of 21732, so it counts once with it. Nikon 2691 ('St. Methodius says') cannot be identified.
findings.fix: Replace 21617 with 5360 and note the pseudo-Methodius caveat in doubts.

findings.what: All four Nikon passages at 21582-21732 sit inside 'The gloss', a Greek Apocalypse commentary (Andrew of Caesarea's type) that Nikon quotes. They are not Nikon's own sentences. The rule as written allows them, but Mark should know the Russian case leans on a quoted gloss.

why: His own works are held and he founded nothing. Both traditions reach 5 under the rule as written, though the Russian count is thin.

name: Constantine

findings.what: The census window of his home movement opens with his own act ('Between Constantine's toleration of the church in 312 and ...'). The draft says only 'founded no census movement' and does not raise this. He did not found a movement in the ruling's sense, but the point belongs in doubts.
Elias 3175 is a bare reign-list entry. It counts, but it is the weakest of the seven.

why: Documents issued in his name are held in Eusebius, and both later traditions have 7 distinct passages that clearly name Constantine I.

name: Eunomius of Cyzicus

rejected.(all 11 refs): tradition not later: Hieronymian starts 382, but Eunomius was alive and active until c. 393 (exiled by Theodosius; Jerome's own De viris illustribus of 392 says he 'is said to be still living in Cappadocia')

findings.what: Fails the 'later' test for hieronymian-ascetic-literary. last_year 360 is only the year he became bishop. Jerome's own text on the counted shelf says he was still living when Jerome wrote (392). Socrates V.20 and Michael the Syrian have Theodosius (379-395) send him into exile. The Hieronymian tradition (census start 382) overlaps his lifetime, so only Syriac counts and he does not reach two later traditions.
findings.fix: Mark as not passing unless a second later tradition (e.g. Palaiologan, Justinianic) is counted strictly to 5.

findings.what: dates gives no end date and the candidate's last_year (360) is wrong: he was active under Theodosius and died in exile c. 393. The Library sources for this are Socrates V.20, Michael the Syrian and Jerome's DVI.
findings.fix: Give him as active 360 to after 383, died in exile under Theodosius; correct last_year.

why: He does not pass the count after the 'later' correction, and the founder question for the Eunomians would send him to Mark anyway.
